title: 1999 HMMT February Oral Problem 1
statement: Start with an angle of \(60^{\circ}\) and bisect it, then bisect the lower \(30^{\circ}\) angle, then the upper \(15^{\circ}\) angle, and so on, always alternating between the upper and lower of the previous two angles constructed. This process approaches a limiting line that divides the original \(60^{\circ}\) angle into two angles. Find the measure (degrees) of the smaller angle.

solutions.text:
The fraction of the original angle is \(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{8}-+\cdots\). This is just a geometric series with first term \(1 / 2\) and ratio \(-1 / 2\), so the sum is \(1 / 3\). Therefore the smaller angle is \(20^{\circ}\).

Score 20 points for the correct answer, 5 points for a correct justification. Just setting up the sum is worth 6 points, getting \(1 / 3\) is worth 9 more.
